newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bank shares hit by MGAM woes. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank shares hit by MGAM woes. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Deutsche Bank were sharply lower in afternoon trade on Monday as the market sought to digest recent troubles at the MGAM asset management wing of Germany's biggest bank.

In afternoon IBIS DAX trade the share was among the biggest losers at 71.49 marks, down 54 pfennigs or three quarters of a percentage point, with the overall IBIS DAX up 0.71 percent at 2,567.85 points.
The bank (Corrrects from "The market") described earlier rumours that a Deutsche Bank board member was to step down as "total nonsense".

Dealers said shares were hit by the news that Deutsche Bank's treasured triple-A credit rating was under examination by Moody's Investors Service to assess the implication of the situation at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management.

Last week, Deutsche's Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) temporarily suspended three of its funds and an urgent investigation into possible "irregularities" was launched in conjunction with regulatory authorities.
Dealers were divided on the implication of the incident on the books balance sheets, with some dealers forecasting losses of up to a billion marks and others describing the impact as "peanuts".
